sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: The file proposes changing the default (per the file) behavior when closing upgradeable (per the file) programs so that program accts are fully reclaimed and (per the file) their addresses become reusable. Per the file, tombstoning program accts would remain supported, but (per the file) only when explicitly requested. sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, today, closing an upgradeable (per the file) program permanently tombstones its program acct, preventing reuse of the program ID. Per the file, this behavior has led (per the file) to several issues: Loss (per the file) of funds: Users frequently (per the file) confuse close program with (per the file) close buffer in the (per the file) Solana CLI, unintentionally irreversibly disabling programs. Per the file, permanent acct bloat: Tombstoned program accts cannot be reclaimed and (per the file) accumulate indefinitely in the accts database. Per the file, rPC performance degradation: getProgramAccounts (per the file) against the loader v3 (per the file) program must return all program accts, including closed ones, increasing (per the file) response size and latency. Per the file, these drawbacks outweigh the (per the file) benefits of mandatory tombstoning. Per the file, a more flexible model lets safe address reuse by (per the file) default while preserving explicit (per the file) tombstoning for users who require it. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

paragraphs: Per the file, the Loader V3 Close instruction is to be updated to include (per the file) an optional boolean input. Per the file, if not provided, the default is to be false. Per the file, the accts required by the instruction (per the file) are unchanged: Account 0: Programdata acct (writable) Account 1: Recipient (per the file) (writable) Account 2: Authority (per the file) (signer) Account 3: Program acct (writable) Currently, the authority (per the file) (index 2) and program (index 3) accts are only required for (per the file) closure of initialized programs. The file also calls for them for reclamation of legacy tombstones. Per the file, this is detailed in (per the file) the Control Flow section.

sections.heading: Base Workflow
paragraphs: Per the file, for a value of (per the file) false, the program will clear the program acct's data, resize it to (per the file) zero, and withdraw all lamports. Per the file, this will render the acct no longer rent-exempt and (per the file) subject to garbage collection by (per the file) the runtime at the end of the tx. Per the file, as such, the program address may be reclaimed after the acct has been garbage collected. Per the file, the Close instruction MUST (per the file) fail if tombstone is (per the file) false and the program (per the file) was deployed in the (per the file) current slot (this field (per the file) is stored in the programdata acct layout). Per the file, this prevents a deploy-close-reclaim (per the file) loop within the same slot, which (per the file) would corrupt the program cache (see (per the file) Security Considerations).

Per the file, programs deployed in the (per the file) current slot can still (per the file) be closed with tombstone=true. Per the file, for a value of (per the file) true, the program will clear the program acct's data, resize it to (per the file) zero, but retain the rent-exempt (per the file) minimum lamports for the base acct metadata. Per the file, the program acct will then be assigned (per the file) to itself, creating a (per the file) permanent tombstone for the program. Per the file, in both workflows, the programdata acct is to be defunded and set (per the file) to Uninitialized, causing it (per the file) to be garbage collected at end of tx. sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: The file removes a harmful default (per the file) behavior that has caused (per the file) repeated loss of funds (per the file) and persistent state bloat, (per the file) while preserving security guarantees (per the file) for users who explicitly (per the file) wish to permanently disable a program ID. sections.heading: Security Considerations
paragraphs: Per the file, the program cache relies on two invariants: **One redeployment per slot**: (per the file) The cache keys on (per the file) program address and deployment slot. Per the file, multiple deployments to the (per the file) same address in one (per the file) slot would corrupt the cache. **Loader stability within a tx**: A program's loader determines (per the file) its ABI and alignment requirements. Per the file, changing loaders mid-tx would cause CPI mismatches. The file preserves both invariants: **Program acct**: When closing without tombstoning, the acct is drained of lamports (per the file) rather than reassigned to System. Per the file, the acct remains owned by Loader (per the file) v3 until garbage-collected at tx end, preventing same-TX redeployment. Per the file, additionally, closing without tombstoning (per the file) is rejected if the (per the file) program was deployed in (per the file) the current slot, preventing (per the file) multiple-TX loops. **Programdata acct**: Fully deallocated and reassigned to System.

Per the file, this is safe because (per the file) programdata is not used (per the file) for cache indexing or (per the file) invocation. **Tombstone**: When tombstoning, the program acct is assigned to itself, (per the file) permanently locking the address. Per the file, self-owned accts cannot be modified.
